title: Clear messages, the right tone and calls that get results

say: Clear messages, the right tone, and phone calls that get results.
This is the video for module 1 of Business Communication.
Your reader often sees your message on a small phone screen, between other tasks. If they cannot see quickly what you want and by when, your message waits.
So the first habit is to say what you want early.

panel.heading: Three habits behind every good message
items: Use plain words and short sentences
Match your tone to the reader
Use the phone well, then confirm in writing

say: The second is plain words. Clear writing is not about big English.

say: Before you type, ask: who is reading this?

panel.heading: Plan a clear message in four moves

say: Then ask: what exactly must they do?

panel.heading: Plan a clear message in four moves

say: Now put the purpose and the request in the first one or two sentences. Keep the greeting, but keep it short.

panel.heading: Plan a clear message in four moves

say: Finally, check and cut. Aim for sentences of about 15 to 20 words, with one idea in each.

panel.heading: Plan a clear message in four moves

say: Watch out for phrases like do the needful, or kindly revert. They hide the real action. Say please send the signed form, or please reply by Friday.

panel.heading: Plan a clear message in four moves
panel.rule: Name the exact action and a date. Not "do the needful".

say: For example, Funke runs an events business in Ibadan and needs the hall manager to send an invoice.
Her first message was 68 words, with the request hidden at the end and no date, hall name or number of guests.

panel.heading: Funke's message to the hall manager
left: Request hidden at the very end
No date, hall or number of guests
right: Name and phone number at the end

say: Her new message is 45 words. Please send me the invoice for the Main Hall for Saturday, for about 120 guests, by Wednesday.
The manager can act without calling back.

panel.heading: Funke's message to the hall manager
left: Request hidden at the very end
No date, hall or number of guests
right: Name and phone number at the end

say: Think of formality as a ladder. At the top are banks, government and anyone you contact for the first time. Write in full sentences, with no emojis.

panel.heading: The higher the step, the more formal

say: Next come new clients and partners. Be polite and complete, with a little warmth.

panel.heading: The higher the step, the more formal

say: Regular suppliers and customers can be friendly and short, but still clear on details.

panel.heading: The higher the step, the more formal

say: Team members get brief messages, but still with the task and deadline.
When unsure, start one step higher, then follow their lead.

panel.heading: The higher the step, the more formal

say: Firm is not the same as rude. For example, Amina's 50 tote bags from a printer in Kano were due on Monday. It is now Wednesday.
A message that is too soft reads as not urgent.

panel.heading: Amina chases a late delivery

cards.d: "Sorry to disturb you, maybe you can check on the bags?" The printer reads it as not urgent.
Capital letters, insults and threats. The printer becomes defensive and the relationship is damaged.
Order number, the date it was due, why it is urgent, a clear deadline and a direct question.

say: A message that shouts and threatens makes the printer defensive, and damages the relationship.

panel.heading: Amina chases a late delivery

say: The firm message gives the order number, the due date, the reason it is urgent, a deadline of Thursday 5pm, and asks for a reply today.
Facts, effect and next step. That gets a real delivery time, not an excuse.

say: Answer with three things: a greeting, your business name and your own name. Good morning, Bisi's Bakes, this is Bisi speaking.

panel.heading: Answering a business call
items: Greet, give the business name and your name
Close and say what happens next

say: Listen to the full request without interrupting.

say: Repeat the key details back. So that is two dozen cupcakes for Friday at 10am?

say: Agree the next step: the price, the payment method and the delivery time.

say: Close politely and say what happens next, for example, I will send the invoice on WhatsApp in ten minutes.

say: When you make a call, write three lines first: who you are, why you are calling, and what you need. Then confirm the agreement in a written message straight after.

panel.heading: Answering a business call
items: Greet, give the business name and your name
Close and say what happens next
panel.rule: The call is not finished until the agreement is in writing.

say: Keep business voice notes under about one minute, main point first, recorded somewhere quiet. Send numbers and addresses in text too.

panel.heading: Voice notes: do and avoid
left: Main point in the first sentence
Keep it under about one minute
Send numbers and addresses in text
right: Several long voice notes in a row
Prices or account numbers only in audio
Sharing BVN, PIN or OTP on a call

say: And protect your money. Never share your BVN, card PIN, OTP codes or banking password on a call. Banks do not ask for these. End the call and phone your bank on the number on your card.

say: To remember. Put your purpose and request at the top. Name the exact action, date, amount and place. The newer or more senior the reader, the more formal you write. Be firm with facts, never rude. And confirm every phone agreement in writing.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Purpose and request in the first one or two sentences
Name the exact action, date, amount and place
Newer or more senior reader: more formal
Firm means facts, effect and next step
Repeat details back and confirm calls in writing

say: Now practise. Rewrite one real message you sent, and count the words before and after. Place ten business contacts on the formality ladder. Then script one real call, and send a written follow-up within one hour.
